flags.why: Bare phồng describes swelling or blistering rather than naming a blister.
Nổi phồng is unnatural in this sentence.
flags.fix: Tay anh ấy bị phồng vì cầm cuốc cả ngày. = His hands blistered from holding a hoe all day.

flags.why: The example explains the unit's composition instead of showing it in use.
flags.fix: Binh đoàn này đóng quân ở miền Trung. = This corps is stationed in central Vietnam.

flags.why: Quê mùa disparages someone's appearance or sophistication and can offend when applied to a person ([dictionary](https://loigiaihay.com/tu-dien-tv/que-mua-ebbwtUz4TpnlR.html)).
The example defines the anatomical term instead of showing it in use.
flags.fix: Bệnh nhân bị đau ở hậu môn. = The patient has pain in the anus.

flags.why: Công chuyện is used mainly in Southern Vietnamese.
The example explains what a solar eclipse is instead of showing the word in use.
flags.fix: Chúng tôi đã xem nhật thực sáng nay. = We watched the solar eclipse this morning.

flags.why: This pun is used disparagingly for Muslims and needs a warning beyond slang and Internet ([usage example](https://www.reddit.com/r/VietNamNation/comments/1qspfku/ae_ngh%C4%A9_sao_v%E1%BB%81_c%C3%A1i_c%C3%B2m_n%C3%A0y/)).
Mặn meaning funny or witty is common in contemporary informal usage, so rare is misleading.
Mặn expressing ardent affection belongs to literary usage rather than ordinary colloquial speech.
Tình yêu của hai người rất mặn is unnatural for the intended sense of ardent affection.
flags.fix: Hai người vẫn mặn tình với nhau. = The two remain deeply attached to each other.
